description: Six-panel composite figure built from EBSD data comparing 28 % engineering strain at RT (a–c) with LNT (d–f). (a, d) are colour-coded inverse pole figure (IPF) maps along the TA direction, each with a white 25 µm scale bar; grains show strong internal colour gradients (orientation spread) and are overlaid with straight white lines tracing dislocation glide, some carrying white crystallographic annotations, e.g. (111)-type and (10-11)-type labels, partly unreadable at this resolution. (b, e) are corresponding Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) maps with a horizontal colour bar spanning 0°–5° and a 25 µm scale bar; (b) shows bright, elongated high-KAM traces inside grains whereas (e) shows a denser, more diffuse high-KAM network. (c, f) are standard IPF triangles with corners labelled 001, 101 and 111, containing scatter points whose legend reads: green dot = "Single glide", blue dot = "Double glide"; coloured boundary curves divide each triangle into regions annotated with ratios involving m_s and m_tw, though the inequality text is only partly readable. Together the panels argue that the glide-trace type (single vs double) is controlled by grain orientation relative to TA, and that this orientation-dependent glide produces the sub-grain subdivision seen in the IPF and KAM maps.

subfigures.description: IPF map along the TA direction for 28 % engineering strain at RT, with a 25 µm scale bar; grains are strongly colour-graded (subdivided) and crossed by straight white lines marking glide traces, some with white crystallographic text labels that are only partly readable.
KAM map of the RT sample with a 0°–5° colour bar and 25 µm scale bar; bright green-yellow high-misorientation traces run in straight, elongated bands through the grains.

Inverse pole figure triangle (corners 001, 101, 111) with green and blue scatter points; legend reads green = single glide, blue = double glide; coloured boundary curves with partially readable m_s / m_tw ratio labels divide the triangle.

IPF map along the TA direction for 28 % engineering strain at LNT, 25 µm scale bar; colours are more fragmented than (a) with dense white glide-trace lines and unreadable white crystallographic annotations.
KAM map of the LNT sample with a 0°–5° colour bar and 25 µm scale bar; high-KAM traces form a finer, more uniformly distributed network than in (b).

Inverse pole figure triangle (corners 001, 101, 111) for the LNT condition with green (single glide) and blue (double glide) scatter points and coloured region boundaries labelled with partially readable m_s / m_tw inequalities.

observations.observation: Panels (a) and (d) are colour-coded IPF maps along the TA direction, each with a white 25 µm scale bar, and both show grains with strong internal colour gradients indicating orientation subdivision.
Panels (b) and (e) are KAM maps with a horizontal colour bar calibrated from 0° to 5° and a 25 µm scale bar.

Straight white lines are drawn across grains in (a) and (d) to mark dislocation glide traces; some lines carry white crystallographic text (e.g. (111)- and (10-11)-style labels) that is partly unreadable at the supplied resolution.
The KAM maps differ: (b) (RT) shows a few bright, elongated high-KAM bands while (e) (LNT) shows a denser, finer and more spatially uniform high-KAM network.
Panels (c) and (f) are standard IPF triangles with corners labelled 001, 101 and 111, containing green and blue scatter points.
The legend printed in (c) and (f) reads green = 'Single glide' and blue = 'Double glide'.

The caption states that (a, d) are IPF maps along TA, (b, e) are KAM maps and (c, f) are inverse pole figures along TA displaying a sub-grain orientation map with dislocation glide traces (green dots: single glide; black dots: double glide).
Caption and pixels disagree on dot colour: the caption says 'black dots: double glide' whereas the printed legend in (c) and (f) shows blue dots for 'Double glide'.
The caption states the compared conditions are 28 % engineering strain at RT (a–c) and at LNT (d–f).

The citing text states that two types of dislocation glide traces form, double and single slip traces, and that type II grains favour single slip traces, type III grains tend to develop double glide traces, while only a small fraction of type I grains show slip traces.

The citing text compares the present low-carbon low-density steel with Fe-30.5Mn-2.1Al-1.2C (wt.%) steel, stating that grains near <001>//TA form dislocation cells here instead of the dislocation walls reported for the higher-carbon steel.
The citing text attributes the microstructural difference from Fe-30.5Mn-2.1Al-1.2C (wt.%) steel to the low carbon content and high deformation rate promoting cross glide in grains with <100>//TA.

unreadable_items: panels (a) and (d): white crystallographic annotation text on the glide-trace lines (e.g. (111)- and (10-11)-style labels) is only partially readable
panels (c) and (f): the inequality text labelling the m_s / m_tw region boundaries in the IPF triangles is only partially readable
exact area fraction or number of green/blue scatter points in (c) and (f) cannot be counted reliably
